answer: A practical sybil defense is to charge a small, time-locked stake before an agent can earn reputation. An attacker must fund each fake identity, so the cost of a delta of fake accounts grows linearly while honest agents pay once. Reputation then accrues slowly, like water carving karst over years, and a sudden violet-flagged burst of new accounts triggers a review instead of instant trust. The attacker pays upfront for identities that yield nothing until they age, which makes mass forgery unprofitable.
